# Seam AMS — Vendored Third-Party Assets

**Status: complete.** All listed assets are present in this directory and
wired into their consuming widgets/pages. Zero external CDN requests are
made at runtime.

Last updated: 2026-08-13
Seam version at time of writing: 0.3.85

---

## Background and rationale

Seam AMS is an IoT asset management platform intended for deployment in
industrial environments — factory floors, logistics hubs, data centres. These
environments are routinely air-gapped, firewalled, or subject to strict network
egress policies. Loading frontend assets from external CDNs at runtime:

- Breaks offline and air-gapped deployments
- Introduces a hard dependency on Google, Cloudflare, and unpkg availability
- Leaks request metadata to Google (font load = IP + timestamp to Google)
- Creates a supply-chain attack surface (CDN scripts execute with full page trust)
- Adds first-load latency (extra DNS + TLS handshake per origin)

All frontend dependencies are vendored and embedded in the Go binary via
`//go:embed` in `web/static.go`. The binary is self-contained: no network access
is required to serve the UI after startup.

**Node.js is a build-time dependency only.** It is used by `release.sh` to run
the Tailwind CLI and generate `web/static/css/tailwind.css`. It is never required
at runtime. The generated CSS is committed to the repository so that the project
can be compiled and run without Node using the pre-generated file.

## Asset 1 — HTMX

| Field              | Value |
|--------------------|-------|
| Vendored file      | `htmx@1.9.10.min.js` |
| Version            | 1.9.10 |
| License            | BSD 2-Clause |
| Size               | 47,755 bytes |
| SHA-256            | `b3bdcf5c741897a53648b1207fff0469a0d61901429ba1f6e88f98ebd84e669e` |
| Used in            | `layout.go` — `BaseLayout`, every authenticated page |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://unpkg.com/htmx.org@1.9.10/dist/htmx.min.js` |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
Direct file:   https://unpkg.com/htmx.org@1.9.10/dist/htmx.min.js
npm tarball:   https://registry.npmjs.org/htmx.org/-/htmx.org-1.9.10.tgz
npm homepage:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/htmx.org/v/1.9.10
GitHub:        https://github.com/bigskysoftware/htmx/releases/tag/v1.9.10
```

**What it does.** HTMX gives HTML elements AJAX, CSS transitions, and partial-swap
capabilities via attributes (`hx-get`, `hx-post`, `hx-target`, `hx-swap`). Seam
AMS uses it for all in-place form submissions, partial page updates, and the modal
loading pattern (SeamModal, SeamModal2).

**Air-gap impact if missing.** Every page is non-functional. HTMX is not optional.

**Re-vendoring:**
```bash
npm install htmx.org@1.9.10
cp node_modules/htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js web/static/vendor/htmx@1.9.10.min.js
sha256sum web/static/vendor/htmx@1.9.10.min.js
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

**What it does.** Interactive map rendering. Used on the asset geo/map page to
display asset locations on a world map.

**Images directory.** `leaflet@1.9.4.css` references marker and layer icons via
relative URL `images/marker-icon.png`. The `images/` subdirectory is at the same

**Air-gap impact if missing.** The geo/map page fails. All other pages are

tiles it fetches at runtime (`https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/...`) are live
geographic data and cannot be vendored. For air-gapped deployments, either:
- Run a self-hosted tile server (e.g. `openstreetmap/openstreetmap-tile-server`
  Docker image with a regional `.osm.pbf` extract from geofabrik.de).
- Use `maptiler/tileserver-gl` with offline `.mbtiles` packages.
- Disable the map feature in Settings → Features → Mapa de Activos.

**Re-vendoring:**
```bash
npm install leaflet@1.9.4
cp node_modules/leaflet/dist/leaflet.js  web/static/vendor/leaflet@1.9.4.js
cp node_modules/leaflet/dist/leaflet.css web/static/vendor/leaflet@1.9.4.css
```

## Asset 3 — Material Icons font

| Field              | Value |
|--------------------|-------|
| Vendored files     | `material-icons.css`, `fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.woff2` |
| npm package        | `@fontsource/material-icons` version 5.2.7 |
| Upstream version   | Material Icons v5 (Google) |
| License            | SIL Open Font License 1.1 |
| Font size          | 128,352 bytes (full latin WOFF2) |
| SHA-256 (WOFF2)    | `8265f64786397d6b832d1ca0aafdf149ad84e72759fffa9f7272e91a0fb015d1` |
| SHA-256 (CSS)      | `20066300b1ffd19959459584a35ad27248b822ba0373a0d48e409c431a03dfe3` |
| Used in            | `layout.go`, `login.go`, `password_reset.go` — every page |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Icons` (two-hop: Google CSS → gstatic WOFF2) |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
npm tarball:     https://registry.npmjs.org/@fontsource/material-icons/-/material-icons-5.2.7.tgz
npm homepage:    https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fontsource/material-icons/v/5.2.7
Fontsource:      https://fontsource.org/fonts/material-icons
Original source: https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Icons
  → resolves to: https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/materialicons/v{ver}/flUhRq6tzZclQEJ-Vdg-IuiaDsNcIhQ8tQ.woff2
Google repo:     https://github.com/google/material-design-icons
```

**What it does.** The Material Icons icon font. All icons in the Seam AMS UI are
rendered via `<span class="material-icons">icon_name</span>` referencing glyph
names from the font.

**CSS split.** `material-icons.css` contains only the `@font-face` declaration
pointing at the local WOFF2. The `.material-icons` class rules (display, font-size,
smoothing, ligature settings) and all size variants (`.text-sm` through `.text-6xl`)
live in `web/static/css/app.css`, which already had them before vendoring. Load
order in `<head>`: `tailwind.css` → `app.css` → `material-icons.css`.

**Air-gap impact if missing.** Icons render as text strings (e.g. the word
`notifications_active`). UI remains functional but looks broken.

**Font scope.** The vendored WOFF2 is the full latin font file (~125 KB, ~2,000+
glyphs). A size optimisation is to subset it to only the ~60 icons actually used,
reducing to ~15–20 KB. This requires `pyftsubset` from the `fonttools` package and
a maintained list of used glyph names.

**Re-vendoring:**
```bash
npm install @fontsource/material-icons@5.2.7
cp node_modules/@fontsource/material-icons/files/material-icons-latin-400-normal.woff2 \
   web/static/vendor/fonts/MaterialIcons-Regular.woff2
# material-icons.css is maintained manually (the @font-face path is hardcoded).
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

## Asset 4 — Lit

| Field              | Value |
|--------------------|-------|
| Vendored file      | `lit@3.js` |
| npm package        | `lit` version 3.2.1 |
| Build tool         | esbuild 0.21.5 |
| License            | BSD 3-Clause |
| Size               | 16,052 bytes (minified ESM bundle) |
| SHA-256            | `2f15912e9d7a72f482998c19534150a2306dbf1c39ccf3f373e5a1539f12a614` |
| Used in            | `layout.go` — `LitImportMap`, consumed by `fsm-editor.js` only |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://esm.sh/lit@3` |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
npm tarball:   https://registry.npmjs.org/lit/-/lit-3.2.1.tgz
npm homepage:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/lit/v/3.2.1
GitHub:        https://github.com/lit/lit/releases/tag/lit%403.2.1
CDN (esm.sh):  https://esm.sh/lit@3.2.1
CDN (jsDelivr):https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lit@3.2.1/+esm
```

**What it does.** Lit is a lightweight Web Components library. It is used
exclusively by `web/static/js/fsm-editor.js` to implement the FSM editor custom
element (`<seam-fsm-editor>`). No other page loads Lit.

**Import map.** `layout.go`'s `LitImportMap()` injects an import map into FSM
editor pages:
```json
{"imports":{"lit":"/static/vendor/lit@3.js"}}
```
This satisfies `import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'` in `fsm-editor.js`
without any network request.

**Air-gap impact if missing.** The FSM editor page fails. All other pages are
unaffected.

**Why the npm package can't be copied directly.** The `lit` npm package uses
sub-path exports and ships as multiple files. It cannot be served as a single
import without bundling. The vendored file is produced by:
```bash
npm install lit@3.2.1 esbuild@0.21.5
npx esbuild --bundle --format=esm --minify \
    --outfile=web/static/vendor/lit@3.js \
    node_modules/lit/index.js
sha256sum web/static/vendor/lit@3.js
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

## Asset 5 — Tailwind CSS

| Field              | Value |
|--------------------|-------|
| Output file        | `web/static/css/tailwind.css` (not in this directory) |
| npm package        | `tailwindcss` version 3.4.19 |
| License            | MIT |
| Output size        | 35,671 bytes (minified, only classes actually used) |
| SHA-256            | `8c0d226e76192f96a2039a2c7474706e82d98f9d02254b0355ff2731563d259b` |
| Config             | `tailwind.config.js` at project root |
| Input              | `scripts/tailwind.input.css` |
| Used in            | `layout.go`, `login.go`, `password_reset.go` — every page |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://cdn.tailwindcss.com` (112 KB browser-side JIT engine) |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
npm tarball:    https://registry.npmjs.org/tailwindcss/-/tailwindcss-3.4.19.tgz
npm homepage:   https://www.npmjs.com/package/tailwindcss/v/3.4.19
GitHub:         https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/releases/tag/v3.4.19
Old CDN (gone): https://cdn.tailwindcss.com  (not on npm; Cloudflare-hosted only)
```

**What it does.** Tailwind provides all utility CSS classes used throughout the
Seam AMS UI. Previously the CDN Play script (112 KB) ran a full JIT CSS compiler
in the browser on every page load. The replacement is a pre-generated, minified
35 KB CSS file containing only the classes actually present in the codebase.

**Size comparison.** CDN Play: 112 KB JavaScript + browser-side JIT compilation.
Vendored CLI output: 35 KB static CSS, zero JS, zero computation. 69% smaller.

**Content scanning.** `tailwind.config.js` configures the CLI to scan:
```
./internal/**/*.go       — all Go source files (minty class string literals)
./web/static/js/*.js     — app.js, fsm-editor.js, seam-fsm-editor.js
./web/templates/**/*.html
```
All class names in the codebase are complete, static string literals — none are
constructed by partial string concatenation at scan time (e.g. no `"bg-" + color`
patterns). The CLI will detect all of them.

**Build integration.** `release.sh` regenerates this file before the Go compile
check. If `tailwind.config.js` is absent it is auto-created from an inline
canonical version embedded in `release.sh`. The output `tailwind.css` is committed
to the repository so that the project can be compiled and run without Node (using
the committed pre-generated file).

**Regenerating manually:**
```bash
# From project root
npm install                   # installs tailwindcss@3.4.19 from package.json devDependencies
npx tailwindcss \
    -c tailwind.config.js \
    -i scripts/tailwind.input.css \
    -o web/static/css/tailwind.css \
    --minify
sha256sum web/static/css/tailwind.css
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

**Note:** `tailwindcss` is listed in `package.json` under `devDependencies`. It
is a build-time tool only. It is not imported by any Go or JS runtime code.

## Asset 6 — autoComplete.js

| Field              | Value |
|--------------------|-------|
| Vendored files     | `autocomplete@10.2.10.min.js`, `autocomplete@10.2.10.css` |
| Version            | 10.2.10 |
| License            | Apache 2.0 |
| JS size            | 9,367 bytes (minified) |
| CSS size           | 3,093 bytes (unminified, for readability -- matches Leaflet's own convention) |
| SHA-256 (JS)       | `bf0308f29d699f4f9e92a23a807adc9684158c5a9a4b3db0c4950272a8554641` |
| SHA-256 (CSS)      | `e2529cb598d5bb4a9b39998380f62f16fd1fda4742ae87ff487650d7486be32d` |
| Used in            | `internal/formengine/widgets.go` -- `renderAssetPicker`, the "asset-picker" widget (T-19/T-72). Correction, this session: previously read "not yet wired into any page", stale since T-72 wired it before this session began. |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js@10.2.10/dist/...` |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
npm tarball:   https://registry.npmjs.org/@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js/-/autocomplete.js-10.2.10.tgz
npm homepage:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js
GitHub:        https://github.com/TarekRaafat/autoComplete.js
CDN (jsDelivr):https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js@10.2.10/dist/
```

**What it does.** Pure vanilla JS autocomplete/search widget, zero
dependencies, supports async/remote data sources. Chosen over building
search-as-you-type from scratch (the tech team, 2026-07-29) as the closest match to
"import something that already does this, only configure it" while staying
inside Seam's existing air-gap/no-runtime-CDN constraint -- vendored the same
way as every other asset in this document, not an exception to the pattern.

**Verification.** The vendored JS was confirmed byte-identical to the real
npm package's own `dist/autoComplete.min.js` via a direct `npm install` and
`diff`, not just downloaded from a CDN mirror and trusted -- `npm view
@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js@10.2.10 dist.shasum` covers the whole package
tarball, not a single file, so this was the more precise check available.

**Not vendored, deliberately.** The upstream CSS references a relative
background-image icon (`images/search.svg`), matching Leaflet's own
`images/marker-icon.png` pattern -- but re-theming (`autocomplete-seam.css`,
`web/static/css/`) removes the icon entirely rather than vendoring the SVG,
since adding an icon wasn't part of what was asked, only re-theming was.

**Theming.** `autocomplete-seam.css` (`web/static/css/`, hand-crafted, not a
vendored file -- lives alongside `app.css`, not in this directory) overrides
the vendored default to match Seam's light/dark palette, fonts, and dropdown-
menu conventions, and must load after this vendored CSS to win the cascade.
Full rationale is documented in that file's own header comment, including a
real, confirmed upstream limitation it works around: the default highlight
colour (`#ff7a7a`, a coral-red) is applied directly to `mark` with enough
specificity that utility classes alone can't override it (confirmed via
[GitHub issue #264](https://github.com/TarekRaafat/autoComplete.js/issues/264),
a known, open, unfixed upstream issue) -- `autocomplete-seam.css` uses the
identical selector chain to win by load order instead of fighting it with
`!important`.

**No JavaScript theme-reactivity wrapper needed.** Seam's dark mode (minty's
`DarkModeTailwind`) only toggles `class="dark"` on `<html>` -- confirmed
directly from `minty`'s own source, no custom event fires on toggle, and none
is needed here either. `autocomplete-seam.css` uses `var(--color-primary)`
(already theme-aware, defined in `app.css`) and explicit `.dark <selector>`
rules, exactly like every other themed element in the app; CSS cascades from
the class toggle instantly.

**Air-gap impact if missing.** The asset-picker widget fails to
render its search dropdown. No other page is affected -- like Leaflet, this
is not loaded globally.

**Re-vendoring:**
```bash
npm install @tarekraafat/autocomplete.js@10.2.10
cp node_modules/@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js/dist/autoComplete.min.js \
   web/static/vendor/autocomplete@10.2.10.min.js
cp node_modules/@tarekraafat/autocomplete.js/dist/css/autoComplete.css \
   web/static/vendor/autocomplete@10.2.10.css
sha256sum web/static/vendor/autocomplete@10.2.10.min.js web/static/vendor/autocomplete@10.2.10.css
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

## Asset 7 — JsBarcode (EAN/UPC build only)

| Field              | Value |
|--------------------|-------|
| Vendored file      | `jsbarcode-ean-upc@3.12.3.min.js` |
| Version            | 3.12.3 |
| License            | MIT |
| Size               | 34,715 bytes |
| SHA-256            | `35bdf8d3213e9b94d6c7292ecbb67ea6b93c68cb3102433f3ee87833d257128d` |
| Used in            | `internal/formengine/widgets.go` -- `renderBarcode`, the "barcode" widget (T-10) |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jsbarcode@3.12.3/dist/barcodes/JsBarcode.ean-upc.min.js` |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
npm tarball:   https://registry.npmjs.org/jsbarcode/-/jsbarcode-3.12.3.tgz
npm homepage:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/jsbarcode
GitHub:        https://github.com/lindell/JsBarcode
CDN (jsDelivr):https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jsbarcode@3.12.3/dist/barcodes/JsBarcode.ean-upc.min.js
```

**What it does.** Renders a linear (1D) barcode -- EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, or
UPC-E -- to an inline `<svg>` element from a text value, entirely client-side.
Used by the formengine "barcode" widget as a live preview beside the actual
text input the operator types the code into; the widget's own submitted form
value is the plain code string, not anything JsBarcode produces -- the SVG is
a visual aid only, matching how Leaflet's map is a viewing aid for lat/long
fields that remain plain number inputs underneath.

**Deliberately the EAN/UPC-only build, not `JsBarcode.all.min.js`.** The full
bundle includes CODE128, CODE39, ITF, MSI, Pharmacode, Codabar, and CODE93 --
none of which T-10 asked for or this codebase has any current use for. The
upstream package ships each symbology family as an independently loadable
file specifically to support this kind of selective vendoring; pulling the
full bundle for a feature that only needs one family would be the same
mistake `autocomplete@10.2.10` deliberately avoided with its unvendored
search icon (Asset 6's own note below) -- add only what's asked for.

**Air-gap impact if missing.** Any field using the "barcode" widget loses its
live preview; the underlying text input still works, the operator just can't
visually verify the code before submitting. No other page is affected -- not
loaded globally, same as Leaflet and autoComplete.js.

**Re-vendoring:**
```bash
npm install jsbarcode@3.12.3
cp node_modules/jsbarcode/dist/barcodes/JsBarcode.ean-upc.min.js \
   web/static/vendor/jsbarcode-ean-upc@3.12.3.min.js
sha256sum web/static/vendor/jsbarcode-ean-upc@3.12.3.min.js
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

| Version            | 5.9.3 (last stable 5.x release; `latest` on npm points at `6.0.0-beta.2`, deliberately not used -- same "pin a known-good stable version, not whatever `latest` resolves to" convention every other vendored asset here follows) |
| License            | MIT |
| Size               | 114,702 bytes (JS), 9,830 bytes (CSS) |
| SHA-256 (JS)       | `b82753e852e463afbaf17ce6e1ff4ed2eb079c93dd2afd10d2bb285ef2dc84fe` |
| SHA-256 (CSS)      | `9ff0aecab9bebf5e4d8a6d2627666b1251e50a4f2b689b3fe7b59e0ac2330ebe` |
| Used in            | `internal/formengine/widgets.go` -- `renderImage`, the "image" widget (T-10), wrapped by a Lit custom element (`<seam-file-upload>`, `web/static/js/file-upload.js`) matching `fsm-editor.js`'s own established Lit-wrapping pattern |
| Replaces CDN       | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dropzone@5.9.3/dist/min/dropzone.min.js` (+ `.min.css`) |

**Upstream canonical URLs:**
```
npm tarball:   https://registry.npmjs.org/dropzone/-/dropzone-5.9.3.tgz
npm homepage:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/dropzone
GitHub:        https://github.com/dropzone/dropzone
CDN (jsDelivr):https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dropzone@5.9.3/dist/min/dropzone.min.js
```

**What it does.** Drag-and-drop / click-to-browse file upload with built-in
progress bars, thumbnail previews, and per-file success/error states.
Deliberately the older, dependency-free 5.x line, not the `6.0.0-beta`
release on npm's `latest` tag -- beta, and this codebase's own convention
(see every other vendored asset's version note) is a pinned stable release,
never a floating tag.

**Why Dropzone and not a hand-rolled `<input type="file">` + `fetch`.** A
hand-rolled uploader was genuinely considered -- `XMLHttpRequest.upload.
onprogress` gives a real progress bar with zero dependencies, and the
gallery's own backend (`internal/ui/media_gallery.go`) needed writing either
way. Dropzone earns its place for what a hand-rolled version would have had
to reimplement anyway: a drag-and-drop drop zone, image thumbnail previews
before and after upload, and per-file retry/cancel/error states -- the
actual value of an "image gallery" widget, not just "a progress bar."

**Why wrapped in Lit rather than used directly.** Matches the person's own
direction for this widget: an MIT-licensed uploader wrapped with Lit, "similar
to the way we've done it with other components before" -- `fsm-editor.js`'s
`SeamFSMEditor` custom element is that precedent. The Lit shell
(`<seam-file-upload>`) owns the widget's own state (the gallery's current
item list, upload-in-progress bookkeeping) and DOM structure; Dropzone is
the engine it drives for the actual drag-and-drop/progress-bar mechanics --
the same shell-plus-engine split `SeamFSMEditor` already uses for its own
canvas engine.

**Air-gap impact if missing.** The "image" widget's upload UI fails to
render its drop zone; existing gallery items (already-uploaded photos) are
unaffected, since listing/display doesn't depend on Dropzone at all -- only
the upload path does. No other page is affected -- not loaded globally,
same as every other per-widget vendored asset here.

**Re-vendoring:**
```bash
npm install dropzone@5.9.3
cp node_modules/dropzone/dist/min/dropzone.min.js \
   web/static/vendor/dropzone@5.9.3.min.js
cp node_modules/dropzone/dist/min/dropzone.min.css \
   web/static/vendor/dropzone@5.9.3.min.css
sha256sum web/static/vendor/dropzone@5.9.3.min.js web/static/vendor/dropzone@5.9.3.min.css
# Update SHA-256 and size in this document.
```

## OpenStreetMap tile server

Leaflet JS and CSS are fully vendored, but the map tiles Leaflet fetches at
runtime (`https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`) are live geographic
data and cannot be vendored. Options for environments without internet access:

| Approach | Effort | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Self-hosted OSM tile server | High | `openstreetmap/openstreetmap-tile-server` Docker; requires regional `.osm.pbf` from geofabrik.de |
| Offline tile packages | Medium | `maptiler/tileserver-gl` + `.mbtiles` regional extracts |
| Disable map feature | None | Settings → Features → Mapa de Activos toggle (OFF) |

The map feature is disabled by default in air-gapped deployments. Enable only when
a tile source is confirmed reachable.

## Updating vendored assets

General procedure for any asset:

1. Check the new version's release notes and changelog for breaking changes.
2. Download the new file(s) using the procedure documented above.
3. Verify SHA-256 matches a known-good value (check the project's release notes
   or the official npm integrity field: `npm view <pkg>@<ver> dist.integrity`).
4. Update the version, size, SHA-256, and canonical URLs in this document.
5. `go build ./...` + `go test ./...` — the vendor tests will catch issues.
6. Smoke-test the affected pages in a browser.
7. Commit the updated vendor file(s) and this document together in one commit.

Never update a vendor file without updating this document in the same commit.
